messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Telugu, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Telugu line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (truth‑condition) | Target Word / Phrase (Telugu) | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|------------------------------------------|------------------------------|------------------------|--------| | In | locative “in” (introduces domain “all parts”) | **లో** (as part of “అన్ని భాగాలలో”) | in | OK | | tutte | universal quantifier “all” | **అన్ని** | all | OK | | parti | set of spatial divisions → “parts” | **భాగాలు** (appears in “భాగాలలో”) | parts | OK | | impera | “governs” – He rules over each part | **పాలిస్తాడు** | governs | OK | | e | coordinates two predicates | *(omitted – comma used instead)* | and | UNNECESSARY | | quivi (1) | locative “there” for the second predicate | **అక్కడ** | there | OK | | regge | “reigns” – holds sovereign authority there | **నిర్వహిస్తాడు** | reigns | OK | | quivi (2) | locative “there” for existence statements | **అక్కడ** | there | OK | | è | copular “is” – asserts existence | **ఉంది** | is | OK | | la | definite article (feminine singular) | *(omitted)* | the | UNNECESSARY | | sua | possessive “his” (refers to Sovereign) | **ఆయన** | his | OK | | città | “city” – the Sovereign’s urban domain | **నగరం** | city | OK | | e (2) | coordinates “city” with “seat” | **మరియు** | and | OK | | l' | definite article (masc. sing.) before adjective | *(omitted)* | the | UNNECESSARY | | alto | adjective “lofty” – qualifies the seat | **ఉన్నత** | lofty | OK | | seggio | “seat” – the Sovereign’s throne | **సింహాసనం** | seat | OK | | oh | vocative interjection “O” | **ఓ** | O | OK | | felice | adjective “happy” – describes the chosen one | **సంతోషవంతుడా** | happy | OK | | colui | pronoun “he” – the individual elected | **అయన** | he | OK | | cu' | relative pronoun “who/whom” introducing clause | *(omitted)* | whom | UNNECESSARY | | ivi | locative “there/thereto” – place of election | **అక్కడ** | there | OK | | elegge | “elects” – He selects the individual there | **ఎన్నుకున్నవాడు** | elects | OK |
---
### Items Not Marked **OK**
| Source Word | Issue | |-------------|-------| | e (first) | Conjunction omitted; Telugu often drops “and” when a comma suffices. | | la | Definite article unnecessary in Telugu. | | l' | Definite article unnecessary in Telugu. | | cu' | Relative pronoun unnecessary; clause is expressed without an explicit pronoun. | | e (second) | (No issue – retained as “మరియు”). | | **All other tokens** are correctly rendered with appropriate gender, number, and case. |
No **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or **GRAMMAR** errors were detected.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Telugu script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Telugu text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
